text: Typical patent timeline in India: Day 0: File application (provisional or complete). Month 18: Application published (or earlier if early publication requested). Month 48: Last date for Request for Examination (RFE). Post-RFE: Examination report (FER) within 1-3 years. After FER: 6+3 months to respond. Post-response: Possible second examination report, hearing, grant. Total: 3-5 years typically. Expedited examination: 120 days target from expedited RFE.

Don't miss these patent deadlines: 12 months: Convention priority claim (from first foreign filing). 12 months: Complete specification (from provisional filing). 18 months: Publication (automatic; earlier if requested). 48 months: Request for Examination (from priority/filing date). 6+3 months: FER response (from FER date). 3 months: Appeal against refusal. 12 months: Post-grant opposition (from grant publication). 18 months: Restoration of lapsed application. Annual: Renewal fee payments. Annual by June 30: Working statement (Form 27).

PCT international application timeline: Month 0: File PCT application (directly or from national application within 12 months). Month 16: International Search Report (ISR) issued. Month 18: PCT application published. Month 22: Demand for International Preliminary Examination (optional). Month 28: International Preliminary Report on Patentability (if demanded). Month 30/31: National phase entry deadline in most countries (some allow 32). Post-national entry: follows each country's prosecution timeline.

Trademark registration timeline in India: Day 0: File application. Week 1-2: Application number assigned. Month 3-6: Examination, objections (if any). Month 6-12: Show-cause hearing (if objections not resolved). After examination: Publication in Trade Marks Journal. 4 months: Opposition period (from publication). Post-opposition (if none): Registration certificate issued. Total: 18-24 months typically. Opposed cases: additional 2-3 years.

Design registration timeline in India: Day 0: File application. Month 1-3: Examination for novelty and formal requirements. If objections: 3 months to respond. After clearance: Registration certificate issued. Publication: Design Journal. Total: 6-9 months for straightforward applications. Renewal: initial 10 years, extendable by 5 years (apply before expiry). Post-15 years: Design enters public domain.

Copyright registration timeline: Day 0: File application online (copyright.gov.in). 30 days: Mandatory waiting period for objections. Month 2-3: Examination, clarifications if needed. Month 3-4: Registration certificate issued (if no issues). Note: Copyright exists automatically upon creation — registration provides evidence, not the right itself. Fast process compared to patents/trademarks.

NBA approval timeline for IP applications (Form III): Day 0: Submit application to NBA. Week 1-2: Application acknowledged. Month 1-3: Initial review, clarifications sought if needed. Month 3-4: NBA meeting to consider application. Month 4-6: Approval letter issued (with benefit-sharing conditions). Total: 3-6 months typically. Apply well before patent filing deadline. Some complexity may extend timeline.

Patent opposition timelines: PRE-GRANT OPPOSITION: Any time after publication, before grant. No fixed deadline, but file early for best effect. POST-GRANT OPPOSITION: Within 12 months of grant publication in Patent Journal. Response time: 2 months for counter-statement. Evidence: 1 month for opponent's evidence, 1 month for patentee's reply. Hearing: scheduled after evidence completion. Decision: 1-3 months post-hearing typically.

Patent renewal payment schedule: Year 2: No separate fee (included in filing). Years 3-20: Annual fee due on filing anniversary. Grace period: 6 months after due date (with additional fee). Lapse: If not paid within grace period, patent ceases. Restoration: Within 18 months of lapse (with petition, fee, and showing unintentional lapse). Set reminders 2-3 months before due date. Pay in advance (up to 4 years) for convenience.

IP litigation timelines (approximate): Interim injunction: 1-6 months from filing (urgent cases faster). Trial completion: 2-5 years (Commercial Courts Act aims for faster). Appeal: 1-3 years (High Court), 2-5 years (Supreme Court). Total from filing to final: 5-10+ years in contested cases. Alternative: mediation/arbitration — can resolve in 6-18 months. Factor time into enforcement strategy.

CDSCO regulatory timelines for AYUSH: Classical ASU drugs (Schedule E): Manufacturing license 2-4 months. Proprietary ASU drugs (new formulations): 6-12 months (stability data, safety data required). Clinical trial approval: 3-6 months for protocol approval. Trial completion: varies by protocol (Phase I-III). Marketing approval post-trial: 6-12 months. Plan IP filing around regulatory timeline — file patent before clinical data made public.

FSSAI licensing timelines: Registration (petty food business): 7-15 days. State license (medium business): 30-60 days. Central license (large business, importers): 30-60 days. New ingredient approval: 6-12 months (FSSAI scientific panel review). Renewal: apply 30 days before expiry. Faster than drug approvals, but claims restrictions apply.

Strategic timeline for international patent filing: Month 0: File Indian application (establishes priority date). Month 1-6: Develop international strategy, assess markets. Month 11-12: File PCT application claiming Indian priority (within 12 months). Month 16-18: Receive ISR, assess patentability internationally. Month 22-28: Optional: international preliminary examination. Month 30: Enter national phase in selected countries. Post-30: Prosecute separately in each country. Key: don't miss 12-month priority deadline for PCT or direct foreign filing.

Trade secret protection timeline: Day 0: Information is created. Immediately: Implement confidentiality measures (NDAs, access controls). Ongoing: Maintain secrecy continuously. Forever: Protection lasts as long as information remains secret. Critical moments: employee joins (NDA at hiring), employee leaves (exit reminder), partnership discussions (NDA before disclosure), product launch (assess what remains secret). No filing, no deadline, no expiry — but lost instantly if disclosed.

Patent term considerations: Standard term: 20 years from filing date. Effective term: 20 years minus prosecution time (if grant takes 5 years, only 15 years of enforceable rights). No term extension in India: unlike US/EU, India doesn't extend term for regulatory delays. Strategy: file early, prosecute quickly (expedited examination), maintain renewals throughout term. Plan product lifecycle around 20-year horizon.

Annual IP compliance calendar for AYUSH businesses: January-March: Review portfolio, plan year's filings. April-June: File Form 27 (working statement, due June 30). July-September: Mid-year renewal payments check. October-December: Budget for next year's IP costs. Monthly: Check approaching deadlines (renewals, responses). Quarterly: Review new competitor patents. Annually: Conduct IP audit, update strategy. Set calendar reminders for every deadline — missed deadline can mean lost rights.
